summary: This informational RFC moves RFC 3627, which advised against using /127 prefixes between routers, to Historic status. RFC 6164 updates that guidance, and as a Standards Track document it takes precedence in conflicts.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo marks RFC 3627 as Historic because RFC 6164 superseded its guidance. It explains that the Standards Track document takes precedence if the two disagree.

questions: ipv6 prefix length for router links
which guidance applies to /127 router links
why does rfc 6164 take precedence over rfc 3627
subtitle: Moves the old RFC 3627 guidance to Historic status and points to the newer RFC 6164 guidance.

tldr.problem: RFC 3627's guidance on /127 prefixes between routers was superseded by RFC 6164, but the documents were not clearly linked.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6547 moves RFC 3627 to Historic status and clarifies that RFC 6164 takes precedence where the documents conflict.
tldr.outcome: Readers who consult RFC 3627 are directed to the updated guidance in RFC 6164.

today: RFC 6547 is an Informational memo that obsoletes RFC 3627 and updates RFC 6164. RFC 3627 is Historic, and the memo directs readers to follow RFC 6164 where they conflict.

sections.title: Why RFC 3627 Became Historic
sections.content:
RFC 6547 moves RFC 3627, titled Use of /127 Prefix Length Between Routers Considered Harmful, to Historic status. Its guidance was superseded by RFC 6164, titled Using 127-Bit IPv6 Prefixes on Inter-Router Links.

The RFC says the two documents had not been formally linked, which could confuse readers who did not know how IETF document types interact.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 6164 replaced the guidance in RFC 3627, but the old document did not clearly point to the new one. This memo makes the relationship clear.

sections.title: Which Guidance Takes Precedence
sections.content:
RFC 6547 states that a Standards Track document supersedes an Informational document. Where RFC 6164 and RFC 3627 conflict, the guidance in RFC 6164 is to be followed.

This memo obsoletes RFC 3627 and updates RFC 6164 to link the documents.
sections.plainLanguage: If the two documents disagree, follow RFC 6164. RFC 6547 makes that relationship explicit for readers.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that moving RFC 3627 to Historic status introduces no new security considerations. Its purpose is to link the earlier informational guidance to RFC 6164.
sections.plainLanguage: This document changes the status and cross-reference of earlier guidance. It introduces no new security considerations.
